title: The Orchard of Manchester's mill district
premise: In 1894, Casper Ishikawa keeps the light above Manchester's mill district canal, mourning her husband and hiding her Japanese mother's name behind her English one. When a stranger arrives with letters in her dead friend Thomas's handwriting — a man officially drowned, now branded an enemy for sheltering mill strikers — she learns he is alive, hunted, and dying. Bound by a peacetime promise to hide him, Casper smuggles him through the orchard behind the mill while detectives close in. She chooses justice over law, spiriting him onto a ship at the cost of her post, and ends by keeping his daughter, finally claiming both of her names.
about_author: Vesper Sterling is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing mill workers' letters in northern England. They write historical fiction about people history filed under the wrong names.

chapters.title: The Light That Counts the Hours
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Establishes her routine tending the canal light, her grief for her husband, and her careful erasure of her mother's name. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Door
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. A rain-soaked woman named Ada arrives carrying letters in Thomas Whitfield's unmistakable hand — the man Casper buried five years ago. Beat: disbelief curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Handwriting of the Drowned
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She reveals Thomas is alive, hiding among strikers, and dying of a lung wound; the letters are his plea to Casper specifically. Beat: reluctant hope.

chapters.title: What Was Promised in Peacetime
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, flashback woven in: the promise made on the orchard wall before the strikes turned deadly. Beat: the weight of old vows resurfacing.

chapters.title: The Orchard Behind the Mills
chapters.summary: Casper scouts the abandoned orchard as a route; we learn its history as a workers' meeting place. Beat: quiet resolve hardening into intent.

chapters.title: Detectives in the District
chapters.summary: Inspector Hale's POV. He arrives hunting a fugitive and begins interviewing mill families; his methodical menace contrasts Casper's world. Beat: the net tightening.

chapters.title: First Meeting in the Ruins
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. She finds Thomas alive but feverish in the orchard's root cellar; their reunion is angry, tender, and too short. Beat: grief overturned by guilt and love.

chapters.title: The Price of Keeping Quiet
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Neighbors begin asking questions; Ada lies badly and Casper must cover for her. Beat: paranoia seeping into daily life.

chapters.title: Letters Never Sent
chapters.summary: Casper reads Thomas's cache of unsent letters, learning why he faked his death — he witnessed a mill owner's fatal crime. Beat: moral clarity sharpening.

chapters.title: Hale Calls at the Lighthouse
chapters.summary: Casper's POV under interrogation; Hale notices her foreign surname and probes it cruelly. Beat: identity as vulnerability.

chapters.title: The Fever Breaks, the Secret Doesn't
chapters.summary: Ada's POV nursing Thomas; he confesses the full truth of the crime and the name of the owner's accomplice — someone Casper trusts. Beat: betrayal discovered.

chapters.title: An Ally in the Mill Yard
chapters.summary: Casper recruits mill worker Bridget Flaherty, who owes Thomas her brother's life. Beat: fragile alliance formed in shared risk.

chapters.title: The Trap in the Orchard
chapters.summary: Hale stakes out the orchard after a tip; Casper must lead Thomas out through the storm-flooded canal path. Beat: terror and improvisation.

chapters.title: Storm Season
chapters.summary: Casper's POV during the great storm; the light fails, the district floods, and chaos offers cover — and new danger. Beat: nature as both shield and threat.

chapters.title: The Accomplice's Bargain
chapters.summary: The trusted friend confronts Casper, offering Thomas's safety in exchange for silence about the crime. Beat: temptation and fury.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. She rejects the bargain and commits to exposing the crime through Thomas's testimony, knowing it dooms her position. Beat: irrevocable choice.

chapters.title: Hale Closes In
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. He pieces together the orchard route and sets a final cordon for dawn. Beat: cold triumph before the fall.

chapters.title: The Last Passage
chapters.summary: Climax. Casper, Ada, and Bridget move Thomas through flooded streets under the storm's cover; a confrontation with Hale ends when Bridget produces evidence implicating the mill owner. Beat: sacrifice and reversal.

chapters.title: Testimony at Dawn
chapters.summary: Thomas, dying, gives his deposition to a magistrate sympathetic to the workers; the mill owner's crime becomes public. Beat: justice outside the law achieved inside it.

chapters.title: What the Sea Takes
chapters.summary: Thomas dies aboard the ship that will carry him home; Casper keeps his promise by taking charge of his daughter, whom Ada has secretly raised. Beat: grief transmuted into family.

chapters.title: Two Names
chapters.summary: Casper loses her post but gains a household; she restores her mother's name alongside her married one. Beat: identity reclaimed.

chapters.title: The Orchard in Spring
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Casper's POV. The orchard blossoms again as workers replant it; Casper, Ada, and the child tend the trees where everything began. Beat: memory honored, future planted.
